text:
Once a change is judged, TextOS proposes topics in a fixed, repeatable way: no language model and no paid call are involved, and running the proposal again leaves it unchanged. That matters when the same change is looked at twice: you get the same suggestion, not a new one each time.

What a future article may lean on is narrow on purpose. TextOS lets only word-for-word public limits or claims already approved in the product profile into the material the writer may use. The engineer's own explanation of a change is treated as the reason it was picked, and TextOS never reads it as permission to publish. So a confident line in a pull request does not end up, unchecked, on your website.
